source_name: Mastercard Global Vendor Certification Program (GVCP) — certified card manufacture / personalisation / provisioning vendors
why_relevant: The scheme's certification regime is itself a supplier directory: only GVCP-certified vendors may manufacture/personalise Mastercard cards for issuers. Determines which personalisation bureaus can serve Hungarian issuers. FAQ is public; the certified-vendor listing itself sits behind Mastercard Connect.

source_name: Visa Global Registry of Service Providers
why_relevant: Searchable registry of Visa-registered/validated service providers (processors, gateways, personalisation, hosting). Filtering by country surfaces providers serving the Hungarian market and their validated service categories — a direct competitor/vendor map for payments infrastructure services.

source_name: Mastercard Newsroom Europe (press releases, HU-tagged)
why_relevant: Primary announcement channel for Mastercard's Hungarian bank/fintech partnerships, product launches (biometric, tokenisation) and market data. Partnership announcements name the issuer, the enabling vendor and the technology.

source_name: Mastercard – Év Bankja (Bank of the Year Hungary) award programme
why_relevant: Scheme-sponsored national award; entries and jury write-ups describe bank digital/payment projects in unusual detail, frequently naming implementation partners. A reliable annual harvest of Hungarian bank technology case studies.

source_name: ANY Biztonsági Nyomda Nyrt. – card manufacture & personalisation (BÉT-listed issuer disclosures)
why_relevant: The dominant Hungarian security printer and card personalisation bureau: Mastercard/Visa chip card production, eID, and the Gránit Bank metal-card project delivered jointly with Thales DIS. Being BÉT-listed, it publishes regulated financial and business reports that quantify the card-personalisation segment — a rare disclosed view of a normally opaque hub.

source_name: BÉT (Budapest Stock Exchange) issuer news & BET50 company profiles
source_subtype: exchange disclosure portal + company profile series
why_relevant: BÉT publishes both regulated filings and editorial company profiles. The CARDNET profile alone gives operational scale data (c. 65,000 POS terminals serviced nationwide, bank terminal operation + non-bank transaction services) that is otherwise unpublished; the same channel covers ANY and other payments-adjacent issuers.

source_name: CARDNET Zrt. – POS terminal operation & transaction processing hub
why_relevant: One of the few Hungarian-owned processing/terminal-estate operators serving banks and acquirers; a direct competitor/partner in the same niche as Printec-type terminal service providers. Company-registry profile gives ownership, financials and group structure.

source_name: Nemzeti Cégtár / OPTEN – company register for infrastructure entities (GIRO, KELER, CARDNET, ANY)
why_relevant: Authoritative corporate data (ownership, capital, filed accounts, management changes) for every entity in this cell. Filed annual accounts of GIRO/KELER carry IT capex and material-cost lines that quantify vendor spend even where contract names are redacted.

source_name: Közbeszerzési Értesítő / EKR – Hungarian public procurement notices
why_relevant: Where any Kbt.-covered procurement by state-adjacent infrastructure bodies (MNB group, state-owned entities touching payments) is announced and awarded. The database section exposes searchable notice archives — the systematic route to award notices naming winning IT suppliers. Note: KELER explicitly reports 'no procurement procedures', so coverage of this cell via Kbt. is partial.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség (Hungarian Banking Association) – member directory & press releases
why_relevant: GIRO is an association member; the association's member list, working-group outputs and press releases map the institutional actors and signal collective infrastructure projects (instant payments, fraud data sharing) before vendor selection.

source_name: Portfolio.hu – GIRO Zrt. topic tag feed
why_relevant: Leading Hungarian business daily maintains a persistent tag page for GIRO — a ready-made chronological archive of infrastructure news, project launches and executive changes.

source_name: GIRO Zrt. LinkedIn company page + Profession.hu / karrierportal job postings
why_relevant: Reveals-indirectly: GIRO's job adverts disclose the technology stack, vendor products and in-flight programmes (ISO 20022, specific middleware/HSM/core platforms) long before any contract is published. Same technique applies to KELER and CARDNET postings.

source_name: Worldline Hungary – financial institutions / acquiring processing pages
why_relevant: A localised Hungarian-language presence from a pan-European processing hub targeting Hungarian banks with ATM/POS/eCommerce acquiring processing — a direct competitor in the processing-hub layer and a likely counterparty in future bank outsourcing deals.

source_name: Nexi Central Europe – regional processing hub (incl. Hungary)
why_relevant: States coverage of Hungary among its CEE markets for full issuing/acquiring processing, terminal management and value-added services — the main outsourced processing-hub alternative to in-house bank platforms in this cell.

source_name: Euronet Magyarország (Euronet EFT) – independent ATM estate operator
why_relevant: Largest independent ATM deployer in Hungary and a processing/cash-network operator; both a buyer of ATM hardware/software and a competitor to bank-outsourced ATM management. Its site documents network scale and services.

source_name: Hungarian plastic-card production bureaus (Coimbra Kft., Draftpress Kft., Plasztikgyár)
why_relevant: Second-tier domestic card producers. Mostly loyalty/access cards rather than EMV bank cards, but they define the local competitive floor and occasionally serve bank-adjacent programmes; useful for distinguishing scheme-certified personalisation (ANY/Thales/IDEMIA class) from general plastic-card printing.

source_name: OTP Mobil (SimplePay) corporate blog / newsroom
why_relevant: OTP Mobil is the largest Hungarian PSP (SimplePay, qvik, ~21,000 merchants) and self-publishes partner awards, integration launches and product announcements; single highest-signal vendor/partnership channel in the HU PSP cell.

source_name: SimplePay technical-partner / developer pages
why_relevant: Publishes the list of integrated technical partners (webshop engines, ERPs, POS vendors) — an actor map of the HU e-commerce/payments integration ecosystem, effectively a partnership registry.

source_name: OTP Bank merchant card-acceptance (kártyaelfogadás) product section
why_relevant: Bank-side acquiring proposition of the market leader; shows terminal/POS offering, pricing structure and which PSP capabilities are bundled — useful for competitor positioning and buyer-need mapping.

source_name: Barion Payment Zrt. corporate site (product, pricing, docs)
why_relevant: Barion is the leading independent Hungarian e-money institution / PSP (MNB licence H-EN-I-1064/2013) and a direct competitor-and-partner for payment technology; site carries product, pricing and integration/partner material.

source_name: Prim Online — Barion Payment Zrt. keyword feed
why_relevant: Hungarian tech news wire that republishes vendor press releases verbatim; a practical substitute for Barion's own newsroom, which was not locatable via search.

source_name: Global Payments Hungary — POS terminal / merchant pages
why_relevant: Global Payments took over Erste's POS network in 2014 and is a top-tier HU acquirer; the HU locale pages document terminal portfolio, softPOS and merchant propositions — direct competitive intelligence on terminal estates.

source_name: Worldline Hungary media relations / press releases (hu-hu)
why_relevant: Worldline (incl. former SIX Payment Services) is the largest bank-independent acquirer in Europe, present in HU since 2009 with 11,000+ merchants; its Hungarian-locale press room publishes partnership and merchant-solution announcements in Hungarian.

source_name: SIX Payment Services Hungary legacy site
why_relevant: Legacy HU domain still serving product pages for the Worldline/SIX acquiring business; useful for historical baseline of terminal and acceptance product lines and for detecting migration/rebranding events.

source_name: Euronet Magyarország — sajtóközlemény page
why_relevant: Euronet is a major independent ATM deployer in Hungary and expanding into merchant services; its Hungarian press-release page is the local channel for network, partnership and deployment news relevant to terminal/self-service estates.

source_name: Euronet Worldwide Investor Relations news releases
why_relevant: Group-level, regulatory-grade disclosure of Hungarian and CEE contracts, ATM/merchant-services partnerships and volumes; more reliable and dated than local marketing pages.

source_name: FinTechZone — Elektronikus fizetési megoldások kézikönyve (handbook)
why_relevant: A curated Hungarian directory of electronic payment solutions and providers — effectively a pre-built actor map of the HU PSP/acquiring landscape, ideal seed for glossary and entity resolution.

source_name: Portfolio.hu — bank/fintech coverage and company tag pages
why_relevant: Leading Hungarian business/financial daily; covers acquirer and PSP market moves, Revolut branch licensing, fee changes and M&A with dates and named executives. Tag pages give per-actor timelines.
